claims.statement: Tom Allen received a dispatch from Jem Coyne of Newark, N.J., announcing that Joe Goss had arrived in America.
claims.excerpt: morning Tom Allen received a dispatch from Jem Coyne, of Newark, N. J., announcing thé arriyal in this country of Joe Goss

claims.statement: Tom Allen and Joe Goss fought for £100 a side and the middleweight championship; after 34 rounds lasting 1 hour 52 minutes the battle was declared a draw. The paper prints the year as 1967, but the fight was in 1867.
claims.excerpt: occupying one hour and fifty-two minutes, the battle was declared adraw.

claims.statement: Tom Allen had taken part in no less than nine encounters since his 1867 fight with Joe Goss.
claims.excerpt: in no less than nine encounters since that time

claims.statement: Tom Allen offered to fight Joe Coburn for as much money as he could raise or for nothing, at a place half way between St. Louis and New York.
claims.excerpt: HE WILL FIGHT COBURN for as much money as be can raise or for nothing,

claims.statement: Tom Allen offered to make a glove fight with Joe Coburn for nothing, or for as much as Coburn chose, and bet $500 that he would make Coburn take off the gloves.
claims.excerpt: Allen will make a glove fight with Coburn for nothing, orforas much as he chooses, and will bet $500 that he will make the New Yorker take off the mittens

claims.statement: Tom Allen played a legitimate part in the crib scene from Tom and Jerry at the Theatre Comique, St. Louis, a couple of weeks before April 1876.
claims.excerpt: a legitimate part played by Allen at the Theatre Comigue a couple of weeks ogo.

claims.statement: It was thought probable that Joe Goss would come to St. Louis and that he and Tom Allen would start out on a sparring tour.
claims.excerpt: that he and Tom will start out on a sparring tour

fights.stakes: £100 a side and the middleweight championship
fights.excerpt: occupying one hour and fifty-two minutes, the battle was declared adraw.
fights.notes: Printed date 'March 5, 1967' (OCR); year read as 1867 from context. Place and rules not given in this article.

notes: Mostly a retrospective on Goss's arrival. Coburn challenges are conditional offers, not agreed matches. The 'Manager We: Allen' of the New Adelphi is a different man and is not included.
